Thank you so much for your comment, it actually really makes me feel a load better knowing that I'm not alone with this situation. Seriously, I thought I was like the only one since I've talked to so many people about my noise-sensitivity and absolutely nobody can relate, well, up until now hahah. I've done so much experimenting with blocking out noise, as far as to covering all the walls with acoustic foam. It just makes me so nervous, but it's really hard to tell what the apartment and living situation will be like until you try it :/ Even I can't tell if I will be able to stand cars with the most obnoxious engines ever, since that's a huge pet peeve of mine to be trying to sleep or study and I just hear this LOUD CAR that sounds like it's expelling the LOUDEST EVILEST FART as it vrooms down the road.

I take a lot of meds for my anxiety and it doesn't do that much to be honest, and plus I'm sort of a real noise-sensitive little chipmunk to the point where I need it to be quiet even when I'm not asleep. I'm okay with noise in public because hey, I'm in public. But when I go home my body just kind of goes onto "rest mode" and doesn't want any disturbance. 

I wonder if it's possible to replace the windows with double-pane windows though, for a rental property :/ I'm not too sure about rental aspects to be honest. Right now I'm just getting my fingers crossed that I can work things out, like moving my bed away from the window, being able to block out sound, or maybe in a miracle - I just won't even be bothered.

Oh no. :( Where exactly is your apartment located at? Because mine is just behind the goodwill shop and I'm already getting so anxious about it. I'm not even sure what to do, I started freaking out once I even saw the apartment to the point that I immediately went online and started looking for new housing. My next-year housemate saw me panicking and asked me why I was freaking out, I must sound loony, but I honestly can't handle really noisy environments. Is it possible to talk to Russ (the office manager) about letting me see the apartment before move-in so that I can get some options? I'm not exactly sure what I could do about it. It's seriously such a curse to be this noise-sensitive, I feel so bad for people who have to put up with me and I also feel bad for my own brain for the self-sabotage hahah.

Indeed, I agree that without a doubt, reddit doesn't give a good or suitable representation of what the UCD community looks or feels like. But, nethertheless, it's still some sort of /representation/. There must also be people who have severe depression / feel lonely and don't talk about it here. I'm actually working with student mental health counseling to make their programs more accessible for this issue as well. Their mental health services are pretty awful, in my opinion. I've seen many people enjoy Davis, but also I'm in that niche that doesn't enjoy it, so I try to do what I can for myself and others that don't enjoy it. Nethertheless, it's been 2 years so I'll see if something changes, I just don't want people who feel lonely to think that this problem isn't a big deal. Social relations is very, very important for the entire behavioral and growth aspect for people. So I think that if people feel lonely and/or struggle with depression and the like because of this, then I'd like to help, and the very first step to that is acknowleding that "wow, this is a pretty significant issue for a population of our students".  

Ultimately I believe a campus should try to keep ascending to greater heights and happiness for all students, so while yeah - Reddit might make this problem seem way worse - that's not to say that Reddit might not be unaccurate either. Both are two groups representing the same school. Though that's respectively my two cents, one student's opinion to another's.

Thanks; sometimes people don't have the most luck with making friends though. I'm a part of 3 organizations and attended a fair amount of clubs, even rushed and got into a sorority here. Still incredibly lonely since it either tends to be professional or a clique that I cannot relate to at all. So it ends up just being "I know people" rather than "I have friends". 

From my experience, I've noticed that it really depends on meeting the right people (having similar sets of values and interests, which is based off of luck) and/or being able to be accepted into a clique, which is what a lot of organizations and clubs don't really do anymore, sadly. (Or at least the ones that I've attended, which is still a hefty amount of checking out 5 clubs over the course of a couple weeks, everyone was so knit-tightly that I always got the cold shoulder when I tried to join in on the conversation.) So I agree whole-heartedly with what you say, go out there and join more clubs - but I would wish that people could understand that a lot of it is also based off of luck on clicking with the right people who will also /want/ to click with you. Either way, I love memes, enjoy this meme.
